Research programme

Quantum holography and associative chiral Koszul duality

Ordered collisions, chiral quantum groups, and the relation between boundary operators and bulk theories.

Last updated 13 November 2026 · What changed

This programme studies singular composition with the order of the inputs retained. Its objects include vertex and quantum vertex algebras, differential-module coefficients on configurations of points, and categories of modules with fusion and exchange. The question is associative: it concerns multiplication and modules before passage to a commutator. Lie–commutative chiral Koszul duality supplies enveloping examples; an associative dual must also carry ordered products and their higher coherences.

The geometric construction separates collision from cutting a configuration into disjoint consecutive blocks. Bar and cobar relate multiplication to coherent comultiplication in this setting. Realizing a dual by fields asks for further structure across the collision diagonals, and scalar terms in the original relations can become curvature. The coefficient category, completion, are part of the mathematical data.

A chiral quantum group should describe how modules combine and exchange as their insertion points move. A coproduct that adds levels, a map that adds ranks, and fusion within one fixed-level category have different domains. Comparing them requires a functor with a , a parameter map and coherent unit laws.

Holography as Koszul duality asks for comparisons with an independently defined bulk theory: its boundary operators, its lines as modules of a dual algebra, their endpoint couplings and fusion, and its local operations. Supported abelian constructions give concrete examples of these comparisons. A joint nonabelian theorem remains open, and preparing a state from a gravitational bulk requires additional amplitudes and sewing data.

This edition

What changed since 12 November 2026

This edition adds character and sewing identities, degenerate Virasoro fields, affine state operations and comparisons, and results on the positivity of Liouville kernels.

  1. Siegel–Weil for the hyperbolic genus

    For holomorphic complex VOAs with strongly rational and lattice rank r≥3r\ge3, positive nonvacuum commutant weights give the Siegel–Weil identity absolutely for r>4r>4 and with the specified continuation at r=3,4r=3,4.

  2. The hyperbolic average on marked curves in every genus

    For the same holomorphic class and r≥3r\ge3, the mass average extends to all genera as a formal and locally analytic equality of sections on marked curves, with simultaneous and factor κr,g=1\kappa_{r,g}=1 for r>g+1r>g+1, otherwise 22.

  3. Nonminimal charges fail near large embedded discs

    For every nonminimal charge 0<c<10<c<1, the closed-surface fails near surfaces with a sufficiently large embedded hyperbolic disc, and therefore on Teichmüller space in every sufficiently large genus.

  4. The degenerate field algebra generated by two doublets

    At irrational complex Virasoro parameter, the algebraic degenerate sector sum has finite-input intertwining fields generated by two doublets, with parity-corrected constant exchange and quantum-group invariant fields equal to the Virasoro vacuum algebra.

  5. The native binary operations admit algebraic higher coherences

    For universal polynomial affine cochains of a finite-dimensional Lie algebra over a characteristic-zero field, with invariant symmetric level and nondegenerate shifted form, resolutions retain the native product and specified secondary bracket with all algebraic state coherences, while the configuration-level lift remains open.

  6. A strict dg bi-Galois object for exterior uncurving marks

    Over a characteristic-zero field, for a finite exterior algebra with primitive degree-one generators, an explicit over the dual exterior Hopf algebra implements, by , the monoidal equivalence between the of any two uncurving marks.

  7. Reconstruction from an admissible geometric vacuum

    On a smooth complex algebraic curve, a category-valued configuration system with compatible 𝒪\mathcal O-linear realizations, invertible vacuum comparisons for surjections and disjoint fusion, realized vacua without sections supported on collision diagonals, and empty vacuum ℂ\mathbb C as a unital algebra, reconstructs a unital chiral algebra by the known Beilinson–Drinfeld construction.

  8. Equal scalar data, different current brackets

    The lattice vertex operator algebras of E8⊕︎E8E_8\oplus E_8 and D16+D_{16}^{+} share central charge 1616, full character, ribbon category and isometric weight-one pairings, yet their current brackets differ.

Status

How to read the status marks

Proved and independently checked
A proof has received an independent reading at exactly the stated scope; an explicit finite counterexample has instead been independently recomputed. None of these programme results has yet been refereed or published. Published antecedents are identified separately.
Conditional
The conclusion is proved under an explicitly named hypothesis that remains unproved.
Open problem
The stated construction or comparison remains unresolved.
Published
An existing result in the literature, with its author, source and year given. Its hypotheses remain those of the cited result.
Partly established
A restricted case, a related theorem or an obstruction is established; the full mathematical question represented by the column remains unresolved.
Not yet formulated
No precise version of this mathematical question is formulated for the example.
Refuted as first posed
The proposed form is ruled out by a proved counterexample or obstruction. Any replacement is stated with its own hypotheses.

Established

Reconstruction from an admissible geometric vacuum

Let XX be a smooth algebraic curve over ℂ\mathbb C. Suppose a , varying under arbitrary parameter pullback, 𝒞I\mathcal C_I on every XIX^I, including 𝒞⌀=Vectℂ⁡\mathcal C_\varnothing=\operatorname{Vect}_{\mathbb C}, has coherent pullback functors for all finite-set maps, equivalences for surjections, unit insertions for injections, and symmetric external fusion over disjoint configurations, satisfying composition, iterated-partition and mixed base-change identities. Let its vacua vIv_I come from the , and let FI:𝒞I→QCoh⁡(XI)F_I:\mathcal C_I\to\operatorname{QCoh}(X^I) be compatible 𝒪\mathcal O-linear realizations whose vacuum comparisons for surjections and disjoint fusion are invertible. Require BI=FI(vI)B_I=F_I(v_I) to have no nonzero local sections supported on collision diagonals and B⌀≅ℂB_\varnothing\cong\mathbb C as an algebra with its actual unit. Then BIB_I is a factorization algebra, and its canonical connection and residue operation reconstruct a unital chiral algebra on the right differential module ωX⊗B{1}\omega_X\otimes B_{\{1\}}, with all operadic substitutions. Equivalences preserving these give isomorphic unital chiral algebras. On 𝔸1\mathbb A^1, translation-equivariant input gives the corresponding vertex algebra; an explicitly retained conformal vector and grading are preserved. This is the Beilinson–Drinfeld reconstruction applied to the specified geometric coefficients.

1

The native operations of the affine bulk

Open problem

Let kk have characteristic zero, let 𝔤\mathfrak g be finite-dimensional, let κ\kappa be an invariant symmetric form, and suppose β=κ+Kill𝔤⁡/2\beta=\kappa+\operatorname{Kill}_{\mathfrak g}/2 is nondegenerate. On the universal polynomial affine Chevalley–Eilenberg complex Z=Vκ(𝔤)⊗Λ(cna:n≥0)Z=V^\kappa(\mathfrak g)\otimes\Lambda(c_n^a:n\ge0), construct a configuration-indexed dg system of regular, localized and supported chiral operations that realizes the specified closed degree-minus-two secondary bracket, its full , the native normally ordered product and an independently specified boundary action. Retain joint formal zero modes in the , polynomial positive-energy states, the algebraic sum over energies, ordered mergers and vacuum insertions, and prove every mixed Leibniz, Jacobi and action coherence. Compare this realization with the independently defined , including its prescribed nullhomotopy on separated configurations and compatibility with both nested and disjoint collisions.

Why it matters

A structure on the vector space of states does not specify how insertions move, collide or act on boundary modules. The comparison would identify which higher operations belong to the geometric bulk and whether they agree with the pairing obtained from the boundary construction.

The native binary operations admit algebraic higher coherences

Let 𝔤\mathfrak g be finite-dimensional over a characteristic-zero field, with invariant symmetric κ\kappa and nondegenerate β=κ+Kill⁡/2\beta=\kappa+\operatorname{Kill}/2, and use the algebraic universal affine complex Z=Vκ(𝔤)⊗Λ(cna)Z=V^\kappa(\mathfrak g)\otimes\Lambda(c_n^a). Any closed, , vacuum-normalized, graded-skew degree-minus-two bracket bb restricting to the inverse-β\beta bracket on C∗(𝔤)C^*(\mathfrak g) extends on the algebraic Sc(Z[3])S^c(Z[3]) to shifted Lie operations of arity nn and degree 4−3n4-3n, with the higher operations zero on and on vacuum inputs. For a fixed resolution of the degree-minus-two Poisson operad, the native normally ordered product and bb can both be held fixed, with all algebraic product, bracket and mixed coherences. The product generator has no imposed symmetry or associativity relation; in a resolution containing a degree-minus-three , that cell can be assigned exactly HLbHL_b, where LbL_b is the Leibniz defect. An already specified full shifted Lie family and this first Leibniz primitive can also be retained by a relative resolution; the uniqueness is homotopy relative to those data, at the level of algebraic states.

Moving centralizers and line fusion

Open problem

For a finite-dimensional nonabelian Lie algebra over a characteristic-zero field, with invariant symmetric level form κ\kappa and nondegenerate β=κ+Kill⁡/2\beta=\kappa+\operatorname{Kill}/2, construct a normalized comparison between the moving affine centralizer, its restricted bar dual in the transverse line direction, and line fusion on affine Weyl modules induced from finite-dimensional . Specify the positive-weight and length completions and preserve the full nonlinear , the prescribed product homotopy, native products, the vacuum and both ordered collision maps on all induced states. On three modules, identify the associativity homotopies with the Knizhnik–Zamolodchikov connection and its descendants. Prove continuity for each source energy, output cutoff and Laurent coefficient, including words containing product entries.

Why it matters

The Casimir residue on a fixes only the first part of the comparison. The line construction must also carry the nonlinear homotopies and all descendants through collision and fusion, on explicitly specified completions where the comparison maps and homotopies are continuous.

On suspended words wn=σJE|(σc0H)⊗nw_n=\sigma J_E\mid(\sigma c_0^H)^{\otimes n}, take the identity-linear bar map with this binary component and all of arity greater than two zero; it satisfies F(w0)=w0,F(wn)=wn−s−1wn−1 (n≥1),F−1(wn)=∑j=0ns−jwn−j (n≥0).F(w_0)=w_0,\quad F(w_n)=w_n-s^{-1}w_{n-1}\ (n\ge1),\qquad F^{-1}(w_n)=\sum_{j=0}^ns^{-j}w_{n-j}\ (n\ge0). Every wnw_n has energy one, and its inverse has a nonzero one-letter term s−nσJEs^{-n}\sigma J_E. Thus this particular algebraic inverse is not continuous in the positive-weight completion and its transpose does not preserve the finite-support dual.

New assembly of known results · Antecedents: Loday–Vallette (2012), Proposition 10.2.3; Atiyah–Macdonald (1969), Chapter 1, Exercises 2(i) and 5(i).

Proved and independently checked

Ordinary derived cochains lose Wilson tensor products

Let kk have characteristic zero, let 𝔤=𝔰𝔩2(k)\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{sl}_2(k), and let RR be its defining two-dimensional representation. The ordinary Chevalley–Eilenberg complex C∗(𝔤;R)C^*(\mathfrak g;R) is acyclic, whereas C∗(𝔤;R⊗R)C^*(\mathfrak g;R\otimes R) has a copy of kk in degrees zero and three. Therefore the functor to ordinary derived C∗(𝔤;k)C^*(\mathfrak g;k)-modules cannot be a faithful strong monoidal realization of these Wilson charges: the derived tensor of the two zero images is zero, while the coefficient tensor has nonzero cohomology.

Known · Antecedents: Chevalley–Eilenberg (1948), Theorem 24.1, pp. 117–119.

What the columns mean
Algebra and geometry
The field algebra or geometric coefficient object, with its multiplication, collision maps, exchange and vacuum.
Koszul dual
The dual construction, its curvature and completion, the category in which it lives, and any biduality or complementary-parameter statement.
Module comparison
A functor or equivalence between explicitly defined representation categories, including their weak equivalences and distinguished vacuum objects.
Fusion and exchange
Products of representations at moving points, associators, braiding, and reconstruction from a fibre functor.
Bulk operations
Local bulk observables or a candidate algebra of vacuum endomorphisms, together with higher operations and their boundary action.
Lines and endpoints
Line defects, their endpoint modules and couplings, and flat connections governing their motion.
States and sewing
State spaces and preparation by amplitudes, with the analytic or formal domains needed for gluing.
Physical comparison
Source and Ward identities, parameter normalization, and comparisons with a bulk theory defined independently of the boundary algebra.

Open problem

A comparison preserving the vacuum and its operations

For nonzero-level Heisenberg modules over ℂ\mathbb C, construct an independently defined comparison between negative-current coinvariants and the degreewise completed curved cochain transform on one common localized category, preserving the marked vacuum, translation, rational collision maps and logarithmic transport. Extend the Gaussian endpoint construction to nilpotent vacuum extensions with compatible transport and framing: for two unit charges at level three, increasing-normal-coordinate graph transport around a positive full turn gives e−2πi/3e^{-2\pi i/3}, whereas positive Fock continuation gives e2πi/3e^{2\pi i/3}. An opposite-transport functor or a comparison with the reverse braided target remains to be constructed, together with the comparison preserving of independent local bulk observables. The outgoing collision normalization is taken on the positive-real branch in this phase test.
