Essay

Essay

On the form of meeting

Raeez Lorgat

The subject is what ordered things do when they meet. One wants to compose operators without losing their order, and to follow their singularities as their positions approach. One wants to fuse lines and understand what their ends do on a boundary. The need for a form is already present in the operations that must be performed.

The difficulty appears in a precise place. In the chiral operations of Beilinson and Drinfeld on a smooth curve over a characteristic-zero field, the inputs allow poles at collisions and the output lies on the common diagonal. Their chiral algebra is a Lie object. If a binary operation in this ordinary right differential-module domain is required to be strictly associative, both its triple composites vanish. Give it a local vacuum whose principal-part action is the identity, even on one side, and the whole module vanishes.

This obstruction clears a path by telling us what the form cannot hold. It also offers a temptation: to mistake the boundary of that form for the boundary of the subject. The Lie–commutative duality of Francis and Gaitsgory supplies the associative bar construction on Lie envelopes. It does not supply a general second associative chiral field algebra. The question of associative duality therefore remains a question in its own right.

A form expresses a content under particular conditions. It bears the limits of the question that called it forth. A successful definition need not become the definition of everything nearby. A complex on configurations, a family of fields and a category of representations make different things available to thought. Their relation must be constructed through the operations they carry. No choice of notation makes one of them absolute.

The inner content here is singular composition with order retained, together with the ways of separating, transporting and representing it. Geometry displays where meeting takes place. Fields display its coefficients. A category displays how objects act and combine. A physical theory supplies its observables, boundaries and defects; a prepared state supplies further data for evaluation. These forms stand beside one another. Their equivalence requires a particular map and its inverse.

A spoon and a sieve can both lift from a pot. One keeps the broth; the other lets it pass. Their shapes answer different tasks. Neither becomes a better utensil by taking the shape of the other.

There are two directions in the local picture. Along the complex curve, collision can be singular. Along a transverse real line, one composes in an order. The order of labels can thus remember a direction in space. For a smooth separated complex curve, the derived analytic functions on the ordered collision atlas agree with holomorphic-topological forms on configurations in the curve times the line.

This comparison respects permutations, deletion of labels and external products on separated configurations. Its scope is these function algebras. An identification of arbitrary coefficient systems, including their local units, asks for more. The order is therefore more than an ornament on a formula, while its interpretation as a physical direction still has a mathematical domain.

Positions can collide, and an ordered configuration can be cut into separated blocks. A residue records a collision. Here residue includes the principal part with every normal derivative; it is not merely the scalar coefficient that survives a contour integral. A cut exposes a coproduct: the object on the whole configuration maps to the objects on its blocks. Strong factorization says that this map is an equivalence on the appropriate disjoint locus.

Bar and cobar relate associative multiplication and coherent comultiplication. On the connected ordered coefficient categories, with scalar empty component and the specified augmentation or coaugmentation, they are inverse equivalences. At n labelled positions, a reduced word has length at most n. The comparison has a finite filtration there. No further global elementwise conilpotence assumption is needed. This does not yet identify the result with another physical field algebra.

Even the geometry has more than one useful form. The full atlas keeps all orders; a word construction keeps consecutive cuts. The natural projection from atlas to word need not preserve the tensor product by an equivalence. Already for two separated singleton inputs it can discard a nonzero summand. The word is useful because of what it retains, and its relation to the atlas includes what it forgets.

There are also two kinds of doing nothing. The scalar object supported only at the empty configuration is the unit for disjointness convolution. Tensoring at the same configuration uses the diagonal exceptional tensor, with the dualizing coefficient system as unit. The full-atlas cobar of this system is the unit of the transported tensor on atlas algebras. The word/cut cobar is a different vacuum algebra, the corresponding unit on the word carrier. On separated binary configurations the atlas cobar retains a nonzero coefficient where the cut cobar vanishes. A local vacuum marking carries information at nonempty configurations; the coaugmentation inserts only the empty unit.

A vacuum is not a scalar augmentation either. For the Heisenberg current with nonzero double-pole coefficient, that pole is a nonzero multiple of the vacuum. A unital map preserving field products would have to send it to the same nonzero scalar. Scalar fields have no singular products, so such a character does not exist. The identity field remains present.

The failure of a scalar splitting to preserve multiplication can be retained as curvature. For the free current the normalized dual curvature density is κcTc/2, where κ is the level, c is an odd ghost and T is translation. Within this paired vertex model, the central current pairing becomes a ghost state. The ordinary residue coalgebra constructed from these ghost fields with zero differential forgets the density, and hence the level. The distinction between emptiness and vacuum cannot be repaired by silently discarding this datum.

Now take the two descriptions as far apart as possible. At one pole remove the physical fields and retain only the vacuum and collision geometry. At the other begin with a field theory, its action and a boundary condition. The first isolates what the geometry itself requires. The second asks what an independently specified system actually does. Neither pole gains authority by reducing the other to an illustration.

On the half-space ℂ×ℝ≥0 take scalar superfields Φ,η of total degrees zero and one, the differential D=d_t+∂̄ and the quadratic action Sκ=τ(ηDΦ+κη∂_zη/2), where τ integrates against dz/(2πi). Impose i*η=0, with i the boundary inclusion, on the whole superfield. The exact Gaussian perturbative quantization has the universal Heisenberg algebra as its finite-energy boundary algebra. Normal-ordered products of derivatives of the current give the fields of all polynomial states. Bulk observables with separated normal support act on the retained boundary complex by continuous cochain operations.

Fix the quantum parameter to one and take the abelian level κ to be nonzero. A Wilson line can end at the boundary through a junction whose period comparison preserves current fields, rooted collision residues and local vacuum. This uses the rotation-finite junction sector and algebraic differential graded line modules. The separated comparison uses a coefficientwise Laurent completion; on bounded complexes of finite sums of scalar charge sectors it compares fusion.

A Gaussian transverse model with secondary pairing −1/κ has a strictly unital homotopy-coherent collision into its jet completion. After shuffle and symmetrization, its scalar bar twist agrees exactly with its line twist. Comparison of this monoid and its action with the native Heisenberg tower remains open.

In the abelian model with positive Schouten normalization, 1/κ appears three times. It is the degree-minus-two bracket of the surviving odd bulk class with itself. Multiplied by scalar charges q and q′, it is the residue of their line connection. The same pairing gives the exponent of the endpoint block, whose counterclockwise half-continuation has phase exp(πiqq′/κ). Here a transposition identifies the bracket with the line residue.

Transport of operations is the inverse transpose of state transport; on scalar charge sectors the phases are opposite. For unit charges at level three, an explicit graph transport along increasing normal coordinates has a closed-loop phase inverse and unequal to that of positive Fock continuation. A braided identification requires the corresponding reversal or another comparison. In the free case the forms can be laid side by side and compared. Their completions, orientations and receiving categories remain part of what is compared.

The equality of the poles is expressed by such correspondences. An order of labels can express a transverse direction. In the free-current coupling, the square of the ghost charge is minus the curvature’s zero mode. Reading this as the current two-point function evaluated on ghosts is a physical dictionary that enters no proof. A homotopy of products can be a residue. None asserts that all the surrounding categories have been identified.

Look now at the order 1, 2, 3. Habit makes the consecutive pairs easy to read: first 1 with 2, or first 2 with 3. The pair 1 with 3 looks misplaced. It can seem like a dash inserted where the sentence does not need one. But the middle position has not ceased to exist. The outer collision asks what happens across it.

In the reduced word/cut cobar of a strong cut coalgebra, the coefficient at n positions is a shifted local-cohomology object supported where every consecutive gap has an equality crossing it. At three positions that supporting locus is exactly the diagonal where the first and third coincide. The second may remain separate or may join them. That locus includes the triple diagonal.

After transporting their full principal parts to the same normal-contact module, the three routes in a compatible system of residues obey

L − R + N = 0.

Here L means that the first two meet first, R that the last two meet first, and N that the outer pair meets first and its result then meets the middle. Writing h for the outer residue, its differential in the two-term field complex is −N=L−R. This is the homotopy between the consecutive products. The residue complexes and their attaching maps carry it.

The same construction gives higher associative operations. For the first-cut transfer, the operation on n≥2 singleton inputs is the outermost residue, with suspension fixed. For general inputs in the field complexes, finite sums over trees remain. With nonidentity field exchange in a compatible residue system, reaching the outer partner requires every intervening exchange before taking the principal part. Associativity is therefore heard at three positions, and coherence continues beyond them. Two-point multiplication alone does not display this witness.

Return to the abstract pole and the scalar vacuum’s word/cut cobar. On a smooth separated geometrically connected curve over a field of characteristic zero, it has nonzero coefficients at several positions. At two points the reduced coefficient lies on the diagonal. At three it lies on the surface where the first and third coordinates agree. The identity fields have no singular operator product, yet the configuration coefficients retain principal parts and their residues.

At four positions the cut vacuum coefficient has a nonzero extension joining its cohomology modules. It is not their direct sum with shifts. Its product from two two-point coefficients, combined by cut convolution, is a nonzero derived morphism inducing zero on every cohomology module. The attachment and the product are distinct facts.

Even this bare object has operations that disappear when one keeps only its cohomology. The vacuum already requires a form capable of retaining a map that acts trivially on cohomology. Its apparent silence comes from the choice of what one listens to.

There is consequently no decision about form that can be made once for every case. There is a decision about what a given case needs. The input can be a Lie-algebra current, a Hopf algebra with a spectral form, a stress tensor or a matrix-valued field. In spectral constructions, compatible coactions belong to a covariant module alongside its fields.

Over k[c,(22+5c)⁻¹], with k a characteristic-zero field and c the central charge, the universal W₃ algebra has a curved quadratic vertex dual with noncommutative ghost fields. Its singular ghost product is nonzero, and its differential squares to the curvature’s zero mode. Nonlinear quadratic relations can require this different form.

Cyclic order can instead produce moments. For universal affine matrix currents at OPE scales κ/K and λ/K, normalized matrix-ordered vacuum traces have a finite expansion in even inverse powers of the rank K. Their planar limit gives noncrossing moments with cyclically ordered blocks. This construction supplies moments; identifying exchange or fusion requires a separate comparison.

On the word carrier, a geometric chiral bialgebra has a coherent coproduct for the transported tensor, with counit to the cut vacuum. A categorical chiral quantum group is a chiral tensor category with specified exchange; a geometric presentation must identify its representation system with that category. Spectral coproducts change level: spectral levels compose in order, and numerical translation levels add. For κ≠0, ordinary diagonal currents in two level-κ tensor factors have level 2κ. Such tensor products differ from fusion at fixed level κ.

Even a free current has two independent ways to change. Take its contraction to be κ/u² + λ/u. The even double pole carries the level. The odd simple pole changes field exchange: on two currents it subtracts 2λ/u times the tensor of the vacua. Exchange is the identity exactly when λ vanishes. In this polynomial family, contraction strength and odd exchange vary independently.

Kernels may live on the additive group, the multiplicative group or an elliptic curve, with their appropriate spectral rings. A function rational in a multiplicative coordinate need not be rational in an additive coordinate. The place where a pole lives belongs to the operation, just as its order does.

A deformation can move the poles themselves. For an even, nonnegatively integer-graded vertex algebra in characteristic zero, with translation raising degree by one and fields respecting the grading, the dilation twist gives a formal quantum vertex algebra. Old translation descendants are expressed by finite differences; a new translation gives ordinary derivative covariance. If degree zero consists only of the vacuum, an original nonzero homogeneous vacuum two-point block of pole order N becomes a rational expression with N simple poles spaced by the deformation parameter. These are poles of the rational block at nonzero parameter; the field algebra is constructed formally.

Dimension changes what can carry the level. For unshifted currents induced from a finite-dimensional Lie algebra on a smooth affine d-fold in characteristic zero, take the central summand to be the canonical differential module shifted by d−1. A central homotopy star-Lie operation of arity n and degree 2−n can occur only when n=d+1. The possible arity is binary on a curve and ternary on a surface; this does not assert existence for every Lie algebra.

In the charged-potential extension of the two-parameter free current, with both parameters and both charges nonzero, a specified charged two-point coefficient has infinitely many linearly independent branches around the puncture. It cannot be the value of a horizontal section of a finite-rank flat bundle under a single-valued meromorphic linear pairing. This obstruction includes irregular bundles.

Global support is another choice. On the total space of the trivial line plus the canonical line over a smooth connected projective complex curve, formal completion along the zero section kills a nonzero compactly supported perfect object on a displaced section, together with its identity. A sector has disappeared before any question of its continuation arises.

The vantage can change from boundary to bulk, from a line to a prepared state. One asks what collides, what acts, what ends and what is prepared. The algebra and its fusion do not by themselves select that preparation. A vacuum insertion, a scalar character and a physical state answer different questions.

The names of the forms can become walls. Bar–cobar duality, coefficient duality, a quadratic field dual, a line-direction bar construction and reflection of parameters are different operations. Internal Homs and endomorphisms of a chosen module add further constructions. Their inputs, variance and units must be named.

A centre must likewise be specified. The convolution centre and the scalar Hochschild centre solve different problems. Vacuum endomorphisms in a chosen category and a universal transverse actor are further objects. Identifying them with independent bulk observables requires comparison. A matching character or scalar residue is insufficient when the next composition uses data that this match has forgotten.

Cohomology can be just such an incomplete image. On the finite Chevalley–Eilenberg complex of a finite-dimensional semisimple Lie algebra in characteristic zero, the degree-minus-two bracket from a nondegenerate shifted invariant form induces zero on cohomology. On cochains it retains the inverse of that form, obtained from the current level by adding half the Killing form. The boundary current products still contain the level.

The affine cochain complex has operations beyond its constant ghosts. For finite-dimensional Lie algebras in characteristic zero and any invariant symmetric level, affine cochains yield a unital transverse monoid acting on affine vacuum coefficients. Its carrier uses joint formal zero modes, polynomial positive-energy states and the algebraic sum over energies. With invertible shifted form, the closed graded-skew degree-minus-two secondary bracket on all universal polynomial affine Chevalley–Eilenberg states has coherent Jacobi homotopies. Lifting this state structure to configuration-indexed geometric operations, with all mixed product and action coherences, remains open.

A comparison is adequate when it carries the operations its purpose consumes. For ordered collisions this includes residues and cuts, the empty unit and local vacuum, the outer homotopy and normal derivatives. One must determine what a forgetful map loses before using its image to identify objects. Then one must carry the whole diagram. The answer can be exact for this case without becoming a prescription for every other case.

There are forms whose comparison is still open. Beyond the constructed quadratic field duals, a general dual with fields and compatible extensions across collisions remains to be constructed. The function-level comparison between ordered configurations on a curve and configurations in the curve times a real line has not become a general comparison of their enhanced coefficient objects with units.

For currents of a finite-dimensional nonabelian Lie algebra in characteristic zero, with invertible shifted form β=κ+Kil/2, its inverse gives the Casimir residue on finite-dimensional charge tops in the Wilson quotient where ghosts and positive modes vanish. The boundary modules are affine Weyl modules induced from these tops. The normalized comparison among the moving affine centralizer, the restricted bar construction in the line direction and line fusion remains open, with its weight and length completions. It must preserve all induced states, nonlinear translation homotopies, native products and three-module coherence.

There remains the joint holographic comparison with an independently defined nonabelian bulk: to prove that its chosen lines are modules of the specified dual, with their endpoints, coupling and fusion, and to identify its local operations on the same terms. Preparing a state from an independently defined gravitational bulk, with regulated amplitudes and sewing, is a further open problem. Each asks for the form in which its still unperformed operation can be made exact.

Glossary

Terms

Definitions of the specialised terms used above. In the text, a term with a dotted underline opens its definition.

Actual component group
For the moduli stack 𝒫\mathcal P of perfect complexes on XX, the group K0semi(X)=π0(𝒫)K_0^{\mathrm{semi}}(X)=\pi_0(\mathcal P) indexes connected components under direct sum. Specifying a class in this group retains more information than specifying only a numerical Chern character.
Admissible geometric vacuum
A realized vacuum diagram assigns a quasi-coherent coefficient sheaf to the vacuum at every finite configuration, with its finite-map, unit-insertion and disjoint-fusion comparisons. Admissibility here requires the stated coherent comparison isomorphisms, no nonzero sections supported on collision diagonals, and normalization of the empty coefficient as an algebra with its true unit. These are geometric hypotheses on the full diagram.
Algebraic cotensor
For a right KK-comodule MM and a left KK-comodule LL, M□KLM\mathbin{\square}_KL is the equalizer of the two coaction maps from M⊗LM\otimes L to M⊗K⊗LM\otimes K\otimes L. The strict algebraic cotensor used here is formed in dg complexes with direct-sum tensor totalization.
Arakawa–Kuwabara–Möller formal sheaf
The ℏ\hbar-adically complete sheaf of vertex superalgebras on HilbN⁡(ℂ2)\operatorname{Hilb}^N(\mathbb C^2) constructed by local framed 𝔤𝔩N\mathfrak{gl}_N BRST reduction of adjoint and fundamental symplectic bosons with fundamental fermions. Its quotient modulo ℏ\hbar is the jet sheaf of the corresponding reduced supermanifold. Formal sheaf cohomology, finite ℏ\hbar-quotients and torus-finite numerical specialization are distinct constructions.
Arithmetic jet
For a prime pp, a δ\delta-ring has a Frobenius lift φ(a)=ap+pδ(a)\varphi(a)=a^p+p\delta(a); the iterates a,δa,δ2a,…a,\delta a,\delta^2a,\ldots are arithmetic jet coordinates. In a pp-torsion-free ring the Frobenius lift determines δ\delta.
Associated lattice
For the holomorphic vertex operator algebras considered here, the Heisenberg charges occurring with the vacuum module of the commutant form a positive-definite even lattice LL. The corresponding lattice vertex algebra is the mutual commutant of the Heisenberg commutant.
Augmentation-generated categories
For an augmented dg algebra HH, thick⁡(k)\operatorname{thick}(k) is generated from the augmentation module by finite cones, shifts and retracts; Loc⁡(k)\operatorname{Loc}(k) also allows arbitrary coproducts. Neither is automatically the whole derived category.
Axion currents
The additional scalar-current families denoted EE and FF in the celestial gauge presentation. Their coupling modifies the current products, and cancellation of the resulting quartic trace tensor is the condition used in the finite quantum quotient.
Barnes-normalized three-point coefficient
For Q=b+b−1Q=b+b^{-1}, let Γb\Gamma_b be the Barnes double-gamma function with periods b,b−1b,b^{-1}, normalized by Γb(Q/2)=1\Gamma_b(Q/2)=1. The coefficient is C0(P1,P2,P3)=Γb(2Q)2Γb(Q)3∏ϵ1,ϵ2,ϵ3=±1Γb(Q/2+i∑jϵjPj)∏j=13Γb(Q+2iPj)Γb(Q−2iPj)C_0(P_1,P_2,P_3)=\dfrac{\Gamma_b(2Q)}{\sqrt2\,\Gamma_b(Q)^3}\dfrac{\prod_{\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2,\epsilon_3=\pm1}\Gamma_b(Q/2+i\sum_j\epsilon_jP_j)}{\prod_{j=1}^3\Gamma_b(Q+2iP_j)\Gamma_b(Q-2iP_j)}.
Becker-coacyclic positive quotient
For a curved ghost contramodule, remove the negative ghost coefficients by the contramodule quotient, including all their summation relations; the result is a dg module over the positive-mode cochain algebra. It is Becker-coacyclic when its Hom complex into every dg module with graded-injective underlying module is acyclic.
Beltrami differential
A Beltrami differential locally has the form μ(z)dz‾/dz\mu(z)\,d\bar z/dz and describes a deformation of complex structure through ∂‾f=μ∂f\bar\partial f=\mu\partial f. For ‖μ‖∞<1\|\mu\|_\infty<1, normalized solutions are quasiconformal maps. Compact support and surface-group periodization specify the actual families used in the closed-surface counterexamples.
Bergman space and fundamental-domain trace
The Bergman space A2(𝔻)A^2(\mathbb D) here is the Hilbert space of square-integrable holomorphic one-forms on the disc. For bounded operators commuting with a torsion-free cocompact group whose disc quotient is a closed surface of genus g≥2g\ge2, integrating the diagonal kernel over one fundamental domain gives the finite group trace, normalized here by τΓ(1)=g−1\tau_\Gamma(1)=g-1. This trace is defined on the equivariant algebra, and need not agree with an ordinary trace on the full Hilbert space.
Bers slice
A Bers slice parametrizes marked quasi-Fuchsian structures while holding the conformal structure of one boundary component fixed. It realizes the other Teichmüller variable in a bounded domain of holomorphic quadratic differentials, with the surface-group equivariance fixed.
Big and generated shuffle algebras
The big shuffle algebra contains the full polynomial or Laurent-polynomial coefficient space in every weight, with its prescribed permutation character and shuffle product. The smaller algebra is the subalgebra generated by weight-one coefficients; wheel conditions can make this inclusion proper.
Browder bracket
For an E3E_3-algebra, the fundamental class of the two-point configuration sphere defines a binary operation of cohomological degree −2-2, called the Browder bracket. Its sign depends on the chosen orientation of that sphere.
cap
A vector or continuous functional assigned to a boundary component filled on one side. In the positive boundary trace model, a cap at inverse temperature β\beta is w(P)e−βHP/2\sqrt{w(P)}e^{-\beta H_P/2}; pairing caps yields the corresponding sewn amplitude.
Cartan extension
The extension of a Hall or shuffle algebra by commuting moment operators prp_r. In the one-loop example, [pr,bs]=br+s[p_r,b_s]=b_{r+s}, and dressing the coproduct by the corresponding Cartan series makes separation of sites compatible with these actions.
Charge top
The finite-dimensional coefficient module from which an affine or Heisenberg module is induced. For a horizontal affine top, 𝔤\mathfrak g acts and positive loop modes act trivially; generalized Weyl induction permits finite jets killed by a sufficiently high power of zz.
Co-vacuum
For a chosen splitting of loop modes into nonnegative and negative powers, the co-vacuum is the module induced from the trivial representation of the negative-mode subalgebra. The usual vacuum is induced from the nonnegative modes; their derived invariants and coinvariants can behave differently.
Coaction-dressed action
For rank-nn RTT series T∗(u)=1+ℏ∑q≥1bqu−qT^*(u)=1+\hbar\sum_{q\ge1}b_qu^{-q}, with Tjl,0∗=δjlT^*_{jl,0}=\delta_{jl}, the action on Koszul cochains is ρM(cij,s)=∑l=1n∑q≥0Tjl,q∗⊗cil,s+q\rho_M(c_{ij,s})=\sum_{l=1}^{n}\sum_{q\ge0}T^*_{jl,q}\otimes c_{il,s+q}. This combines the coefficient-module mode action with the ghost action and converges on the positive weightwise-complete lattices. It is a left BB-action commuting with the ordinary right BB-action.
Cofree conilpotent coalgebra and Taylor components
The algebraic cofree conilpotent symmetric coalgebra on a graded vector space WW is the direct sum of its finite symmetric powers, with coproduct obtained by all splits of the inputs. A coderivation or coalgebra map is determined by its projections from those powers to WW, called its Taylor components. On Sc(Z[3])S^c(Z[3]), a degree-one square-zero coderivation encodes the shifted Lie operations of arity nn and degree 4−3n4-3n on ZZ.
Common-cutoff sewing
Sewing in which all pieces and their common boundary use compatible regulators before any regulator is removed. The boundary identities and their higher compatibility maps must hold for that single regulated construction.
compact smooth kernel carrier
At each fixed number of fields, observables are completed projective bornological tensor powers of compactly supported smooth forms, represented by compact smooth kernels in the corresponding number of variables. The direct sum over field number remains algebraic, so an observable has only finitely many field-number components.
Complete Weil quadratic form
For compactly supported complex g∈L2(ℝ)g\in L^2(\mathbb R), set h(u)=∫g(y)g(y−u)dyh(u)=\int g(y)\overline{g(y-u)}\,dy and Q(g)=∫ℝh(u)(eu/2+e−u/2)du−∑m≥2Λ(m)m(h(log⁡m)+h(−log⁡m))−(log⁡(4π)+γE)h(0)−∫0∞eu/22sinh⁡u(h(u)+h(−u)−2e−u/2h(0))du,Q(g)=\int_{\mathbb R}h(u)(e^{u/2}+e^{-u/2})\,du-\sum_{m\ge2}\frac{\Lambda(m)}{\sqrt m}\bigl(h(\log m)+h(-\log m)\bigr)-(\log(4\pi)+\gamma_E)h(0)-\int_0^\infty\frac{e^{u/2}}{2\sinh u}\bigl(h(u)+h(-u)-2e^{-u/2}h(0)\bigr)\,du, where Λ\Lambda is the von Mangoldt function, γE\gamma_E is Euler’s constant and logarithms are natural. Its extended-real value may be +∞+\infty; its finite-energy domain consists of the inputs for which it is finite.
Consecutive-cut convolution
For a sequence of coefficients on ordered configurations, sum over decompositions into consecutive blocks, take the external tensor product of the block coefficients, restrict to the locus where different blocks are disjoint, and apply derived direct image back to the full configuration space. Its unit has coefficient kk at the empty configuration and zero elsewhere.
Constant ghosts
The constant ghosts are the energy-zero generators c0ac_0^a of the polynomial affine Chevalley–Eilenberg complex. They form the subcomplex C∗(𝔤;k)=Λ𝔤∗C^*(\mathfrak g;k)=\Lambda\mathfrak g^*, with its Chevalley–Eilenberg differential and, for a nondegenerate invariant form, the degree-minus-two inverse-form bracket.
Constant profinite labels
For a profinite set SS, the constant profinite formal scheme over ℤp\mathbb Z_p has coordinate algebra C(S,ℤp)C(S,\mathbb Z_p) of continuous functions, with its pp-adic topology. A label on a test algebra may vary across its idempotent components; it is not required to be one globally constant element of SS.
contact terms
Contact terms are distributional contributions supported where insertion points coincide. The formal source statements fix them through the Cauchy Green operator and the chosen cutoff prescription; separated-point kernels alone do not determine an arbitrary extension.
Coupling modulo total translation
A degree-one coupling II obeys its Maurer–Cartan equation after quotienting states by the image of total translation: QI+12I(0)I=DtotHQI+\tfrac12I_{(0)}I=D_{\mathrm{tot}}H. Since a total derivative has zero zero-mode, this identity can produce a square-zero operator on coefficient modules.
Crossing-normalized RTT double
The matrix-current presentation uses R(x)=1−ℏP/xR(x)=1-\hbar P/x, where PP interchanges the two vector factors, and R‾(x)=g(x)R(x)\bar R(x)=g(x)R(x), with g(x+nℏ)=g(x)(1−ℏ2/x2)g(x+n\hbar)=g(x)(1-\hbar^2/x^2) and g(x)=1+ℏ/(nx)+⋯g(x)=1+\hbar/(nx)+\cdots. The mixed relation uses R‾\bar R with shifts ±Kℏ/2\pm K\hbar/2.
Curved contramodule
A module-like object over a complete curved algebra, equipped with coherent summation operations for coefficient families tending to zero. Its degree-one connection squares to the action of the curvature; a topology on the contramodule itself is additional data.
curved point dual
A curved differential graded algebra has a degree-one derivation dd and a degree-two element hh with d2=[h,−]d^2=[h,-] and dh=0dh=0. For the universal mode algebras here, its continuous Koszul-dual cochains retain the central cocycle as hh; the completion and the module localization are part of the duality data.
Cyclic state
A state or trace functional compatible with cyclic rotation of composable operations and with the proposed sewing maps. A scalar generating series alone does not specify such a functional or its preparation by a cap.
Determinant-torsion classes
For the formal Hilbert-scheme vertex sheaf 𝒟\mathcal D, these are κr=Trβ(ϕψ)\kappa_r=T^r\beta(\phi\psi), where β\beta is the connecting map for multiplication by ℏ\hbar and ϕψ\phi\psi is the classical contraction of the two fundamental fermions. The first class has a logarithmic cocycle representing the first Hodge Chern class of the tautological determinant line. Their generated positive-degree subalgebra is killed by ℏ\hbar; its exterior signs come from sheaf degree, while the intrinsic parity is even.
Discriminant gluing
A positive-definite even lattice LL has finite quadratic group D=L∗/LD=L^*/L, with Q(a)=(a,a)/2modℤQ(a)=(a,a)/2\bmod\mathbb Z. A discriminant gluing identifies this form with the negative of the form labeling the commutant’s invertible modules, so that the paired summands have integral conformal weight; for the stated strongly rational holomorphic class with positive nonvacuum commutant weights, they extend the tensor-product vertex algebra. In a higher-genus amplitude, one such identification acts on every handle.
divided convolution bracket
The convolution bracket on multilinear maps whose target bracket is the graded commutator divided by hh. In the polynomial two-matrix setting that commutator is divisible by hh, so the operation is defined without inverting the parameter.
divided Moyal bracket
For the Moyal product with parameter hh, the bracket bh(f,g)=(f∗hg−g∗hf)/hb_h(f,g)=(f*_hg-g*_hf)/h is polynomial in hh on polynomial inputs, because the numerator is divisible by hh. At h=0h=0 it becomes the Poisson bracket.
Divided-power algebra
ΓR(t1,…,tm)\Gamma_R(t_1,\ldots,t_m) denotes the free divided-power algebra over RR. Its elements γj(t)\gamma_j(t) satisfy γa(t)γb(t)=(a+ba)γa+b(t)\gamma_a(t)\gamma_b(t)=\binom{a+b}{a}\gamma_{a+b}(t), retaining integral versions of tj/j!t^j/j! when the factorial is not invertible.
Empty unit and local vacuum
The empty unit has scalar coefficient kk at the empty configuration and zero elsewhere; a local field vacuum is marked identity-field data at occupied configurations, including vacuum insertions and principal-part identities. The word/cut tensor unit ΩcutJ\Omega_{\mathrm{cut}}J, obtained by cobar from the dualizing coefficient coalgebra JJ, is a separate object. Its tensor-unit property neither supplies a scalar vertex character nor identifies it with a field-vacuum vector.
Endpoint extraction
After gauge transport of a two-position pairing, choose an output coordinate ut=tz1+(1−t)z2u_t=tz_1+(1-t)z_2 and normal coordinate w=z1−z2w=z_1-z_2. Extracting the dwdw coefficient and then normal derivative order zero gives a state operation. The endpoint extractions use t=0t=0 and t=1t=1; their average is distinct from extraction at the midpoint.
energy completion
For a module with generalized energy eigenspaces X[h]X_{[h]}, the energy completion is ∏hX[h]\prod_hX_{[h]}, replacing the direct sum over energies by a product. For a complex, completion term by term is a separate operation from totalization.
Energy retraction
For Z=⨁e≥0ZeZ=\bigoplus_{e\ge0}Z_e with energy-preserving differential, an energy retraction onto A0=Z0A_0=Z_0 consists of inclusion ii, projection pp, and an energy-preserving degree-minus-one map HH, with pi=1pi=1, H|A0=0H|_{A_0}=0, and dH+Hd=1−ipdH+Hd=1-ip. The affine contraction uses division by the positive integer energy on each positive-energy summand.
Energy-additive operation
For a nonnegatively energy-graded complex, an energy-additive operation sends inputs of energies e1,…,ene_1,\ldots,e_n to energy e1+⋯+ene_1+\cdots+e_n. A nullary such operation has energy zero. This grading condition is separate from covariance under translation or geometric support.
finite Weyl filtration
A finite Weyl filtration is a finite filtration whose successive quotients are affine modules induced from finite-dimensional 𝔤[[z]]\mathfrak g[[z]]-modules killed by a sufficiently high power of zz. Its exact structure comes from exact sequences of smooth affine modules.
finite-energy domain
For the two commuting positive Virasoro actions, this is the union of the spectral subspaces on which L0+L‾0L_0+\bar L_0 is bounded above. Each mode acts on this common invariant domain before Hilbert completion.
finite-word vacuum-mode algebra
The actual unital image of finite products of vertex-mode operators acting on the algebraic direct sum of the vacuum algebra's conformal-weight spaces. It has no completion in the mode indices; its curved bar does not by itself classify modules for a completed vertex algebra.
formal source
A source treated through its formal Taylor coefficients, which are multilinear functionals of smooth compactly supported test inputs. A finite-parameter source family is a power series with zero constant term in those parameters. Convergence after assigning numerical parameter values is a separate assertion.
Full algebraic cochains
All linear maps from finite exterior powers of the Lie algebra into the coefficient module, without a support or continuity restriction. For unbounded derived Hom, product totalization retains every component contributing to a fixed total degree.
Full algebraic graded Hom
This Hom complex contains all linear maps of each cohomological degree between the stated algebraic complexes, with differential δf=df−(−1)|f|fd\delta f=df-(-1)^{|f|}fd. No topological continuity, differential-module linearity or geometric support condition is imposed unless separately stated.
Full mixed jet matrix
At a point, the full mixed jet matrix of order mm has entries ∂α∂‾βK\partial^\alpha\bar\partial^\beta K with |α|,|β|≤m|\alpha|,|\beta|\le m, or the congruent Taylor matrix divided by α!β!\alpha!\beta!. Every independent several-variable derivative is included. Restriction to a holomorphic curve instead tests a one-variable matrix and is weaker.
full radical descent
A three-point form descends through a singular intermediate module when it annihilates its entire contravariant radical, including every descendant of every null vector. Sewing through the simple quotient requires this property for both three-point forms.
fusion lattice
A fusion lattice near shifted level κ0\kappa_0 is the module over ℂ[[ε]]\mathbb C[[\varepsilon]], with finite free generalized-energy blocks, obtained by deforming fusion to κ0+ε\kappa_0+\varepsilon and embedding it into the generic fibre over ℂ((ε))\mathbb C((\varepsilon)). Associators and braidings preserve this lattice and specialize by reduction; it need not be the lattice supplied by a generic Weyl basis.
Geometric roof pairing
A roof represents a map after localization by a diagram A←R→BA\leftarrow R\to B whose left arrow is an allowed equivalence. The geometric roof pairing uses a resolving object and its independently defined configuration operations to compare the two pairings. Its nullhomotopy on separated configurations is retained as part of the comparison data.
Grunsky operator
For a normalized univalent map ff, the mixed coefficients of log⁡((f(z)−f(w))/(z−w))\log((f(z)-f(w))/(z-w)), or its differentiated kernel, define the Grunsky operator on a Bergman Hilbert space. In the finite-genus setting here it maps conjugate holomorphic one-forms to holomorphic one-forms, is equivariant for the fixed surface group, and has norm less than one. Hilbert–Schmidt and ordinary trace-class properties must be distinguished from a finite fundamental-domain trace.
Hall occupation currents
On the basis indexed by subsets of finite sites tit_i, let nin_i measure occupation and let cic_i create an unoccupied site and kill an occupied one. The currents are E(u)=∑iciu−ti∏j≠i(1+η/(ti−tj))njE(u)=\sum_i\frac{c_i}{u-t_i}\prod_{j\ne i}(1+\eta/(t_i-t_j))^{n_j} and P(u)=∑ini/(u−ti)P(u)=\sum_i n_i/(u-t_i), expanded at infinity.
Heisenberg commutant
After choosing a Cartan subalgebra of V1V_1, its currents generate a Heisenberg vertex algebra. The Heisenberg commutant consists of the states whose fields commute with these currents, equivalently those annihilated by their nonnegative modes.
Hermitian holomorphic kernel and positive type
A Hermitian holomorphic kernel K(X,Z)K(X,\overline Z) is holomorphic in XX, antiholomorphic in ZZ, and satisfies K(X,Z)=K(Z,X)K(X,\overline Z)=\overline{K(Z,\overline X)}. It is of positive type if ∑i,jaiK(Xi,Xj)aj≥0\sum_{i,j}\overline a_iK(X_i,\overline{X_j})a_j\ge0 for every finite set of points and coefficients. Such a kernel is a Gram pairing of Hilbert-space evaluation vectors.
Hessian obstruction
The adjoint Chevalley–Eilenberg class represented by the cocycle ΩH\Omega_H built from derivatives of the Hamiltonian Hessians. Its nonvanishing prevents an algebraic two-cochain from cancelling that particular cubic residual.
Hopf-link thick subcategory
The idempotent-complete triangulated subcategory of Dcb(S3;ℂ)D_c^b(S^3;\mathbb C) generated by ℂS3\mathbb C_{S^3} and ij∗ℂKj[−1]i_{j*}\mathbb C_{K_j}[-1], where K1,K2K_1,K_2 are the two coordinate circles forming the positively oriented Hopf link and ij:Kj↪S3i_j:K_j\hookrightarrow S^3. It consists of objects obtained from those generators by finite cones, shifts and direct summands.
Identity level
In the finite fusion-operator example, identity level means that the level endomorphism η:H→H\eta:H\to H is idH⁡\operatorname{id}_H. It is a specified datum of that example, distinct from the choice of bicharacter and comodule braiding.
Ind-category and algebraic sector sum
Ind⁡(𝒞)\operatorname{Ind}(\mathcal C) is the category obtained by adjoining filtered colimits to 𝒞\mathcal C. The Virasoro field object here is a direct sum of simple sectors: each state has finite sector support, even though a field output is completed in conformal weight inside its finitely many possible sectors.
Injectivity radius
The injectivity radius at a point of a curvature-minus-one hyperbolic surface is the largest radius on which the exponential map is injective. A disc of any smaller radius embeds isometrically. The large-disc obstruction uses a radius bound at one point, not a lower bound at every point of the surface.
Internally graded Hom
The direct sum over internal weights of homogeneous Hom complexes, with each homogeneous Hom still retaining the products required over source components. Its restricted weight dual and the unrestricted full Hom need not have the same elements or multiplication. For an internally graded space VV, the restricted weight dual is V∨=⨁w(V−w)∗V^\vee=\bigoplus_w(V_{-w})^*.
Lattice genus and hyperbolic genus
A lattice genus consists of lattices isometric over ℝ\mathbb R and over ℤp\mathbb Z_p for every prime pp. For the strongly rational holomorphic class with strongly rational Heisenberg commutant considered here, a hyperbolic genus consists of the holomorphic extensions with that commutant, an associated lattice in the same lattice genus, and the compatible discriminant gluings. Isomorphism classes include the identification of Cartans up to conjugacy.
Leibniz cell
For a degree-zero product μ\mu and degree-minus-two bracket bb, the Leibniz defect is Lb(a;x,y)=b(a,μ(x,y))−μ(b(a,x),y)−(−1)|a||x|μ(x,b(a,y))L_b(a;x,y)=b(a,\mu(x,y))-\mu(b(a,x),y)-(-1)^{|a||x|}\mu(x,b(a,y)). A Leibniz cell is a degree-minus-three operadic generator with differential this defect. Assigning it a homotopy MM with δM=Lb\delta M=L_b realizes the Leibniz identity up to that specified homotopy.
Local simple-current line categories
The finite-length, grading-restricted module categories obtained by local lifts through the simple-current boundary extensions in the abelian mirror construction of Ballin–Creutzig–Dimofte–Niu. In the two-flavour example the charge maps are 1 ↦ (1,1) and 1 ↦ (1,−1); the extension and tensor unit are retained, so these are smaller than all smooth current modules.
long bimodule fibre
For a finite semisimple tensor category with simple objects LiL_i, the long fibre sends MM to ⨁i,jHom⁡(Li,M⊗Lj)\bigoplus_{i,j}\operatorname{Hom}(L_i,M\otimes L_j). The two indices make it a bimodule over ℂI\mathbb C^I; relative tensor product matches the intermediate simple label.
Loop-space factor
The additional factor Hb(ΩG;ℂ)H_b(\Omega G;\mathbb C) in positive-integral derived affine fusion inside the universal-affine category. Passing to the simple-vertex-algebra fusion output applies its augmentation and retains loop degree zero; this does not specify multiplication on all loop-homology classes.
marked collision
A collision operation includes the map obtained when field insertions meet a distinguished module insertion, together with the vacuum insertion and all normal derivatives. Retaining all marked collisions asks for these maps at every finite number of points and their composition identities.
Marked vacuum extension
A marked vacuum extension is a short exact sequence 0→𝟏→iJ→p𝟏→00\to\mathbf1\xrightarrow{i}J\xrightarrow{p}\mathbf1\to0 with its actual injection, projection and a common identification of the unit. Marked charge extensions similarly retain their end modules and maps. Preserving the marking requires intertwining both maps; an unmarked isomorphism of the middle objects is weaker.
Mass of a genus
The mass is the sum of reciprocal orders of the specified finite symmetry groups over the isomorphism classes in the genus. For a lattice it uses the full orthogonal group; for the holomorphic vertex operator algebras here it uses the finite image of the Cartan-preserving automorphism group on the associated lattice, retaining the kernel of its action on the discriminant group.
Meromorphic tensor comparison
Natural comparison maps between tensor products that vary meromorphically with the spectral separation and satisfy coherence where the products are defined. The Drinfeld products here depend on that separation.
Metaplectic convention
The metaplectic group is the double cover of a real symplectic group on which square roots of the determinant automorphy factor can be chosen coherently. Half-integral-weight theta and Eisenstein series use this cover together with the Weil representation; the compatible factors make the combined summand independent of the chosen lift.
Mixed bulk–boundary operations
Operations combining bulk observables, boundary fields and the maps by which the bulk acts on the boundary, indexed by configurations in a space with boundary. Their coefficient objects retain holomorphic collision singularities, composition in the transverse real direction and coherence with vacuum insertions.
Modular torus fibration
The proposed complex threefold maps properly and flatly to ℙ1\mathbb P^1, with smooth fibres complex two-tori, multiple fibres of multiplicities three and four at zero and one, and a reduced non-normal crossing fibre at infinity whose normalization is the degree-six del Pezzo surface. The uniformization, marked period lattice, finite quotient fillings, logarithmic transforms and toric cusp gluing are geometric hypotheses; the underlying smooth topology is a separate question.
Normal convolution
The arithmetic normal carrier retains independent displacements vv and their iterated δ\delta-coordinates around each arithmetic point. Addition of displacements gives a coproduct Δ\Delta on their coordinate algebra HrH_r, and normal distributions multiply by (λ∗μ)(f)=(λ⊗μ)Δ(f)(\lambda*\mu)(f)=(\lambda\otimes\mu)\Delta(f). The finite-weight distributions are ⨁dHomℤp⁡(Hr,dalg,ℤp)\bigoplus_d\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb Z_p}(H_{r,d}^{\mathrm{alg}},\mathbb Z_p), with wt⁡(ti)=pi\operatorname{wt}(t_i)=p^i and wt⁡(wj)=pr−1+j\operatorname{wt}(w_j)=p^{r-1+j}.
Normal-cup product
The operation on sheaf cohomology obtained by combining the Čech cup operation with the vertex-algebra (−1)(-1)-product on local sections. Associativity must be proved on the relevant subspace; the determinant-torsion theorem establishes it on the displayed subalgebra.
normalized modular vacuum amplitude
At central charge c>1c>1, this is Zvac(4π2/β)Z_{\mathrm{vac}}(4\pi^2/\beta), where Zvac(y)=eyc/24∏j≥2(1−e−jy)−1Z_{\mathrm{vac}}(y)=e^{yc/24}\prod_{j\ge2}(1-e^{-jy})^{-1}. It fixes both the vacuum character and its scalar normalization.
normalized Virasoro sphere block
The four-point block obtained by contracting the two highest-vector-normalized three-point Ward forms with the inverse Virasoro Gram matrix at every descendant level. In the first channel it is normalized as Fps(x)=xh(p)−h1−h2(1+O(x))F_p^s(x)=x^{h(p)-h_1-h_2}(1+O(x)), with powers positive on 0<x<10<x<1; the second channel uses 1−x1-x and exchanges the first and third labels.
Null class
A class of complexes declared to become zero in a derived localization. For curved or topological duality, this class must be defined through the actual functors and topology; ordinary acyclicity need not give the required localization.
odd-zero-mode kernel
The kernel of the zero-mode operator of an odd vertex field. In the Hilbert-scheme example the field is χ−=ϕγ\chi^-=\phi\gamma, and its zero mode annihilates exactly the image of the boundary BRST algebra.
Ordered collision construction
Coefficient data over configurations with ordered labels, together with their extensions across collision diagonals and compatibility under cuts and mergers. Keeping a single word order with consecutive cuts and gluing all order charts are distinct constructions.
ordinary vertex-algebra module
An ordinary module has diagonalizable L0L_0, finite-dimensional weight spaces, and weights bounded below in finitely many integral cosets. A grading-restricted generalized module permits generalized L0L_0-eigenspaces under the same finiteness and lower-bound conditions.
Orientation-ratio torsor
The μ2\mu_2-torsor of square-compatible isomorphisms between two orientation lines. Its class in H1(−,μ2)H^1(-,\mu_2) measures whether those fixed square roots can be identified globally.
Parity-corrected two-row fibre
For irrational Virasoro parameter, the two degenerate fusion directions have quantum 𝔰𝔩2\mathfrak{sl}_2 fibres. Their tensor fibre includes the cross-parity correction to braiding and twist, so the two fundamental rows have mixed full monodromy −1-1. Its coherent tensorator is retained when constructing the fields.
Period bundle
A coefficient bundle on an elliptic curve whose pullback to the universal cover has prescribed transformations under the two periods. Those transformations are part of the exchange-field data and must be compatible with its poles, translation and collision operations.
Plumbing and section-valued sewing
Plumbing glues two coordinate discs by zw=qzw=q, with qq the sewing parameter. A formal sewing amplitude is expanded in finitely many such parameters using graded states and their duals. An amplitude continued as a section has the prescribed conformal-anomaly line and coordinate transition laws; it need not be a globally defined scalar function on moduli.
Polarization and diastasis
The holomorphic polarization of a real-analytic potential Φ\Phi is a function F(z,w)F(z,\overline w) whose diagonal is Φ(z)\Phi(z). Its diastasis is D(z,w)=Φ(z)+Φ(w)−F(z,w)−F(w,z)D(z,\overline w)=\Phi(z)+\Phi(w)-F(z,\overline w)-F(w,\overline z), which removes the ambiguity of adding the real part of a holomorphic function to Φ\Phi. The normalization at a base point fixes the remaining holomorphic gauge used in the kernel.
polynomial Fock module
At nonzero Heisenberg level κ\kappa, a polynomial Fock module with zero-mode coefficient space EE is E[x1,x2,…]E[x_1,x_2,\ldots], using finite polynomials. Creation modes multiply by xmx_m, annihilation modes act by mκ∂xmm\kappa\partial_{x_m}, and the zero mode acts on EE.
polynomial ghost algebra
The graded-commutative algebra generated by odd variables dual to Lie-algebra generators and their derivatives, with the Chevalley–Eilenberg differential. Polynomial means finite support in those variables; it does not permit an unrestricted product over the generator labels.
Polynomial line algebra
For a finite-dimensional Lie algebra over a characteristic-zero field, with [xa,xb]=fab cxc[x_a,x_b]=f_{ab}^{\ c}x_c and invariant symmetric form β\beta, the polynomial dg model YβY_\beta has generators ya,ny_{a,n} of degree zero and ηna\eta_n^a of degree one, n≥0n\ge0, with relations [ya,i,yb,j]=fab cyc,i+j[y_{a,i},y_{b,j}]=f_{ab}^{\ c}y_{c,i+j}, [ya,i,ηjb]=−fac bηi+jc[y_{a,i},\eta_j^b]=-f_{ac}^{\ b}\eta_{i+j}^c, and anticommuting η\eta-generators. Its differential is Qηna=12fbc a∑i+j=n−1ηibηjcQ\eta_n^a=\tfrac12 f_{bc}^{\ a}\sum_{i+j=n-1}\eta_i^b\eta_j^c and Qya,n=nβabηn−1b+fab c∑i+j=n−1(ηibyc,j+yc,jηib)/2Qy_{a,n}=n\beta_{ab}\eta_{n-1}^b+f_{ab}^{\ c}\sum_{i+j=n-1}(\eta_i^b y_{c,j}+y_{c,j}\eta_i^b)/2, while translation sends either mode ana_n to nan−1na_{n-1}, with negative-index terms zero. Its elements are finite PBW words; the full restricted bar resolution maps quasi-isomorphically to this model and has additional generators dual to composite PBW entries, which the comparison kills.
Polynomial punctured-space current model
Over ℂ\mathbb C, put An=ℂ[z1,…,zn,u1,…,un]⊗Λ(du1,…,dun)/(∑ziui−1,∑zidui)A_n=\mathbb C[z_1,\ldots,z_n,u_1,\ldots,u_n]\otimes\Lambda(du_1,\ldots,du_n)/(\sum z_iu_i-1,\sum z_i du_i), with d(ui)=duid(u_i)=du_i, d(zi)=d(dui)=0d(z_i)=d(du_i)=0, and Ln=𝔤⊗AnL_n=\mathfrak g\otimes A_n. The regular subalgebra is Pn=𝔤⊗ℂ[z1,…,zn]P_n=\mathfrak g\otimes\mathbb C[z_1,\ldots,z_n], and the negative subalgebra is Nn=𝔤⊗span⁡{uαωn:α∈ℕn}N_n=\mathfrak g\otimes\operatorname{span}\{u^\alpha\omega_n:\alpha\in\mathbb N^n\}, where ωn=∑i(−1)i−1uidu1∧⋯∧duiˆ∧⋯∧dun\omega_n=\sum_i(-1)^{i-1}u_i\,du_1\wedge\cdots\wedge\widehat{du_i}\wedge\cdots\wedge du_n. The internal weights are wt⁡(zi)=1\operatorname{wt}(z_i)=1, wt⁡(ui)=wt⁡(dui)=−1\operatorname{wt}(u_i)=\operatorname{wt}(du_i)=-1; duidu_i has cohomological degree one, and the model uses polynomial functions, algebraic symmetric algebras and ordinary quasi-isomorphisms.
Positive PBW weight and the finite-support dual
For the one-position affine bar, the positive PBW weight assigns 2n+12n+1 to jn=x−n−1j_n=x_{-n-1} and cnc_n, and adds weights in monomials and bar words. Completion allows infinite sums as this positive weight increases. The continuous graded dual has finite support in the completed weight direction, so an algebraic inverse with an unbounded fixed-energy word tail can fail to act on it.
Precisionwise rational exchange
At every finite power of the formal parameter, the exchange has rational coefficients with finitely bounded pole orders on each input. The bound may grow as the precision increases, so the complete output need not belong to an algebraic tensor product with one uniform pole bound.
Principal Virasoro labels
For real c>1c>1, a positive principal label P>0P>0 specifies the highest weight h(P)=(c−1)/24+P2h(P)=(c-1)/24+P^2. The associated positive highest-weight representations form the continuous family used in momentum integration and Hilbert completion; the vacuum is a separate representation.
Principal-parts complex
The homological Chevalley–Eilenberg complex of current-valued rational functions with poles at the insertion points and vanishing at infinity, with coefficients in the tensor product of the inserted modules. Partial fractions separate the underlying vector spaces into local principal parts, while Taylor expansions at the other insertion points enter the mixed differential.
Product-normalized Igusa cusp form
The weight-ten genus-two Siegel cusp form χ10\chi_{10} is normalized here by χ10(y,q,p)=pq(y+y−1−2)∏m≥1(1−qm)20(1−yqm)2(1−y−1qm)2+O(p2).\chi_{10}(y,q,p)=pq(y+y^{-1}-2)\prod_{m\ge1}(1-q^m)^{20}(1-yq^m)^2(1-y^{-1}q^m)^2+O(p^2). The inverse-Igusa series is its reciprocal Fourier expansion in the corresponding positive chamber.
Projective Hilbert space and Fubini–Study form
Projective Hilbert space is the space of complex one-dimensional subspaces of a Hilbert space. For a local nonzero holomorphic vector representative vv, the Fubini–Study form used here is i∂∂‾log⁡‖v‖2i\partial\bar\partial\log\|v\|^2. A holomorphic isometric immersion pulls this form back to the specified Kähler form; projective unitary monodromy means that continuation around a loop acts on its image lines by a unitary operator modulo scalars.
Punctured primitive
A primitive for the Ward or master-equation term on the complement of the singular insertion or divisor. Sewing requires its extension and boundary values to agree across the cuts used to join regions.
Punctured-flow identity
A compactly cut off lift vv of a meromorphic vector-field germ uu generates the formal source flow ∂sμ=∂‾v+vμ′−μv′\partial_s\mu=\bar\partial v+v\mu^{\prime}-\mu v^{\prime}. The Virasoro punctured-flow identity relates the source functional along successive such flows to ordered insertions esT[u]e^{sT[u]} and their central anomaly factor. It determines the contact terms for overlapping cutoffs.
quantum two-matrix BRST complex
The invariant algebra (Wh(𝔤𝔩N⊕︎𝔤𝔩N∗)⊗Λ𝔤𝔩N)GLN/(Tr⁡ψ)(W_h(\mathfrak{gl}_N\oplus\mathfrak{gl}_N^*)\otimes\Lambda\mathfrak{gl}_N)^{GL_N}/(\operatorname{Tr}\psi), with odd ψ\psi of degree −1-1. Its differential is the invariant restriction of h−1[Ω,−]h^{-1}[\Omega,-], where Ω=caμa−12fabdcacbψd\Omega=c^a\mu_a-\tfrac12f_{ab}^{d}c^ac^b\psi_d, {ca,ψb}=hδba\{c^a,\psi_b\}=h\delta^a_b, μ=YX−XY+hNI\mu=YX-XY+hNI, and fabdf_{ab}^{d} are the structure constants of 𝔤𝔩N\mathfrak{gl}_N.
Raw output gauge and diagonal distribution
For an output coordinate uu and translation homotopy KK, the raw output gauge is gu=1+duKg_u=1+du\,K, before adding comparisons between different choices of output coordinate. In the algebraic differential-module direct image along a diagonal, δv\delta v denotes the generator associated to a state vv; zero normal order means that no normal derivatives have been applied to this generator. The midpoint counterexample compares these raw gauges on that generator.
Reduced compact critical coefficients
Vanishing-cycle coefficients for compact moduli of sheaves or perfect complexes after removing the elliptic translation direction. Their comparison requires compatible orientations and maps on actual extension correspondences, beyond the numerical reduced invariant.
Reduced finite-tree bar
The reduced bar cooperad of an augmented operad is built from finite trees decorated by suspended elements of its augmentation ideal. Its differential combines the internal differential and contraction of internal edges; conilpotence means iterated reduced decomposition terminates on each finite tree. The weight-zero quotient used here projects every output factor to weight zero.
reflected-heat propagator
A half-space propagator built from the heat kernels gs(t−t′)∓gs(t+t′)g_s(t-t')\mp g_s(t+t'), using the minus sign for Dirichlet and plus sign for Neumann boundary conditions. One integrates over a heat-time interval [ϵ,L][\epsilon,L] and applies the gauge-fixing differential.
Relative cofibration
A relative cofibration of dg operads retains a specified source operad while permitting homotopically free extensions of its operations. In the concrete cellular presentations used here, generators are adjoined in well-ordered stages and each new differential lies in earlier stages; retracts give the general cofibrations. This is the hypothesis that allows an action to be extended while keeping already specified operations fixed.
Relative smooth localization
Fix the positive-mode Lie subalgebra of a local mode algebra. The semiderived smooth category is the homotopy category of smooth complexes modulo those whose restriction to that subalgebra is coacyclic. Here coacyclic complexes form the smallest triangulated subcategory containing totalizations of short exact triples and closed under coproducts and retracts.
Restricted RTT ghost algebra
For 𝔤𝔩n\mathfrak{gl}_n, this is the completed algebra of odd degree-one generators cij,sc_{ij,s}, s≥1s\ge1, with weight s−1s-1, series c(y)=∑s≥1csys−1c(y)=\sum_{s\ge1}c_sy^{s-1}, differential dc(y)=−c(y)2dc(y)=-c(y)^2 and translation Tcs=scs+1Tc_s=sc_{s+1}. Its relations are cij(y)ckl(y′)+ckl(y′)cij(y)=ℏy−y′(ckj(y)−ckj(y′))(cil(y)−cil(y′)),c_{ij}(y)c_{kl}(y')+c_{kl}(y')c_{ij}(y)=\frac{\hbar}{y-y'}\bigl(c_{kj}(y)-c_{kj}(y')\bigr)\bigl(c_{il}(y)-c_{il}(y')\bigr), with weightwise completion and formal ℏ\hbar of weight −1-1. The restriction on its cochains is decay of sufficiently high mode evaluations modulo every power of ℏ\hbar.
Restricted RTT Koszul cochains
For a positive finite-type RTT lattice MM, the cochains are 𝒦(M)=M⊗ˆB\mathcal K(M)=M\widehat\otimes B, with differential dB+τMd_B+\tau_M, where BB is the RTT ghost algebra and τM\tau_M is the universal twisting cochain evaluated on the Yangian action. The tensor and mode sums use weightwise and ℏ\hbar-adic completion, and sufficiently high mode evaluations lie in ℏNM\hbar^NM for every fixed NN. Arbitrary-value full linear duals need not satisfy this restriction.
Rotation-finite sector
The subspace of vectors whose rotations around the boundary point span a finite-dimensional space. In the boundary and endpoint complexes this selects the algebraic sum of rotation-weight components, rather than an unrestricted product over energies.
Smith exponent
For a Gram matrix over ℂ[[ε]]\mathbb C[[\varepsilon]] that is invertible over ℂ((ε))\mathbb C((\varepsilon)), the Smith exponents are the powers of ε\varepsilon in its diagonal invariant factors. Positive exponents describe the orders at which null directions appear; all positive exponents equal to one means the derivative pairing on the radical is nondegenerate.
Smooth mode module
A discrete module for a local mode algebra is smooth when every vector is annihilated by all sufficiently high positive modes. The cutoff may depend on the vector; a uniform cutoff, an energy grading and finite-dimensional weight spaces are additional hypotheses.
spectral-label pentagon
The pentagon identity for integral kernels that change the internal representation labels in successive fusions. Its validity on label Hilbert spaces does not alone construct a tensor product representing the trivalent Ward maps.
Stable-envelope exchange
A stable envelope maps fixed-point equivariant cohomology into the cohomology of a symplectic resolution after choosing a chamber and polarization. Comparing the maps for two chambers gives an exchange operator on that equivariant coefficient space.
Standard section
A standard section of the induced representation used for an Eisenstein series is a parameter-dependent section whose restriction to the maximal compact subgroup is independent of the parameter. Here the section is fixed by a real Gaussian and finite lattice-coset characteristic functions. Its meromorphic continuation fixes the regularized value before comparison with the genus average.
Strict dg bi-Galois object
A dg bi-Galois object is a dg algebra with commuting left and right Hopf coactions, scalar coinvariants, and invertible left and right canonical Galois maps. Strict means that these maps are actual dg isomorphisms on the specified algebraic complexes. In the exterior example both Hopf algebras are KK.
Strictly plurisubharmonic potential
A real-valued potential is strictly plurisubharmonic when its Hermitian Hessian (∂i∂‾jΦ)(\partial_i\bar\partial_j\Phi) is positive definite. If the potential is real analytic it admits a local holomorphic polarization; positivity of this Hessian alone is weaker than positive type of its exponential kernel.
Strong continuous dual
The vector space of continuous linear functionals, equipped with the topology of uniform convergence on bounded subsets of the original locally convex space. This topology retains convergence information that the algebraic dual does not specify.
Strong cut coalgebra
A coalgebra for consecutive-cut convolution whose coproduct for each cut is an equivalence on the locus where the two blocks are disjoint. Iterated cuts satisfy the coherent coassociativity identities.
Strong orientation data
A square root of the determinant line of self-extensions, together with compatible square-root isomorphisms for direct sums and exact triangles. The compatibility includes associativity over every actual ordered filtration; it is additional structure beyond an isolated square root.
Strongly rational and holomorphic vertex operator algebras
A strongly rational complex vertex operator algebra is simple, self-contragredient, rational, of CFT type V=⨁n≥0VnV=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}V_n with V0=ℂ1V_0=\mathbb C\,1, and C2C_2-cofinite: the quotient by the span of a(−2)ba_{(-2)}b is finite-dimensional. Rationality means complete reducibility of admissible modules. It is holomorphic when its only irreducible ordinary module is itself.
supported localization
A module supported at a finite set SS has, for each vector, a power of PS(t)=∏s∈S(t−s)P_S(t)=\prod_{s\in S}(t-s) whose multiples annihilate it through both current and ghost operations. The supported localization inverts exactly the maps sent to quasi-isomorphisms by smooth induction. This differs from inverting all quasi-isomorphisms of the underlying ghost complexes.
Supported source complex
The observable complex with an additional differential supported on a prescribed line; in the abelian model this term is −iαIL-i\alpha I_L. It specifies the line source on compact tests without asserting that a globally regulated exponential insertion has the same limit.
Tensorator
A tensorator for a strong monoidal functor FF is a natural isomorphism F(X)⊗F(Y)≅F(X⊗Y)F(X)\otimes F(Y)\cong F(X\otimes Y), together with the unit identification, satisfying the associativity and unit coherence diagrams. It is part of the fibre functor used to assemble the degenerate Virasoro fields.
Torus-finite part
The subspace of elements whose torus orbit spans a finite-dimensional representation. For the formal vertex sheaf, this subspace is taken before numerical specialization of the formal parameter; reversing these operations can change the result.
Translation nullhomotopy
A translation nullhomotopy is a degree-minus-one operator KK with dK+Kd=TdK+Kd=T, where TT is translation. This identity does not require KK to be a derivation of the native product. A separate homotopy between two comparison maps has a different defining equation.
Transverse line bar
The bar construction for multiplication along the transverse real direction, formed as the derived relative tensor of two augmentation modules. With diagonal exceptional tensor and dualizing unit JJ, it is J⊗F!JJ\otimes_F^!J for an augmented transverse algebra FF. A line-algebra dual then requires its own restricted or continuous dual and completion.
Truncated multiplication on principal parts
The principal-parts module is Tn=(z1⋯zn)−1ℂ[z1−1,…,zn−1]T_n=(z_1\cdots z_n)^{-1}\mathbb C[z_1^{-1},\ldots,z_n^{-1}]. Multiplication by a regular polynomial is followed by deleting every monomial with a nonnegative exponent in at least one variable; this defines the regular-mode action on the top local-cohomology summand.
Twistor degree
The additive pair of polynomial degrees in the two transverse twistor coordinates. In the finite quantum gauge quotient, J[α]J[\alpha] and E[α]E[\alpha] have degree α\alpha, while J~[α]\widetilde J[\alpha] and F[α]F[\alpha] have degree α+(1,1)\alpha+(1,1); vertex translation leaves this pair unchanged.
Two-boundary kernel
For a closed marked surface of genus g≥2g\ge2, the two arguments specify the conformal structures on the oppositely oriented ends of the quasi-Fuchsian manifold. After choosing a base point, the classical Liouville action determines a Hermitian holomorphic polarization FoF_o; the kernel is Kc(X,Z)=exp⁡(cFo(X,Z)/(24π))K_c(X,\overline Z)=\exp(cF_o(X,\overline Z)/(24\pi)). Its domain here is the whole smooth marked product, without nodal points or a moduli quotient.
Two-copy Heisenberg comparison
Adjoin even free fields t,pt,p and odd free fields η,ι\eta,\iota, with [pλt]=[ιλη]=1[p_\lambda t]=[\iota_\lambda\eta]=1, Qt=ηQt=\eta, Qι=pQ\iota=p, and write a subscript ii for TiT^i. The path substitution is Γs(ui)=ui−κsti+1\Gamma_s(u_i)=u_i-\kappa s t_{i+1}, Γs(ci)=ci−sηi−dsti\Gamma_s(c_i)=c_i-s\eta_i-ds\,t_i; hpathh_{\mathrm{path}} integrates its dsds coefficient, while hcone(a)=∫01∑iιi(∂uia)(u+sp,c)dsh_{\mathrm{cone}}(a)=\int_0^1\sum_i\iota_i(\partial_{u_i}a)(u+sp,c)\,ds. The comparison uses h=hpath−hconeh=h_{\mathrm{path}}-h_{\mathrm{cone}}, the endpoint ϕ(ui)=ui+pi\phi(u_i)=u_i+p_i, ϕ(ci)=ci\phi(c_i)=c_i, and projection PP that kills all auxiliary fields.
Uncurving mark
An uncurving mark specifies the change of differential used to compare a curved or marked module problem with ordinary complexes. In the exterior example, λ∈kr\lambda\in k^r changes DD to D−∑iλiNiD-\sum_i\lambda_iN_i; the weak equivalences are the maps that become quasi-isomorphisms under that particular change.
Unitary minimal charges
The unitary Virasoro minimal charges are c=1−6/[p(p+1)]c=1-6/[p(p+1)] for integers p≥2p\ge2; p=2p=2 is the zero-charge endpoint. The positive minimal charges correspond to p≥3p\ge3. Their appearance in the universal positivity theorem does not by itself settle the fixed-genus kernel.
universal Miura image
The vertex subalgebra generated by the coefficients of the ordered differential operator ∏i=1N(a∂+Ji)\prod_{i=1}^N(a\partial+J_i) inside the universal rank-NN Heisenberg algebra. It retains the universal parameter family; a simple quotient at a special parameter is a separate object.
Universal regular W3W_3
The universally generated PBW vertex algebra with even fields TT of weight two and UU of weight three, normalized so the coefficient of (m−n)Λm+n(m-n)\Lambda_{m+n} in [Um,Un][U_m,U_n] is one, where Λ=:TT:−3∂2T/10\Lambda=:TT:-3\partial^2T/10. The linear and central coefficients use ac=(22+5c)/16a_c=(22+5c)/16, so the weight-three generator and its PBW monomials remain present at c=−22/5c=-22/5.
Vacuum polarization
The splitting of Laurent current modes into the nonnegative modes that annihilate the vacuum and the negative creation modes. The associated ghost representation depends on this splitting and on the finiteness needed for its determinant cocycle.
Ward maps and represented products
A Ward map satisfies the current or stress-tensor Ward identities at its inputs and output; the rational construction includes an output insertion at infinity with restricted contragredience. A represented Ward product is a module with a universal insertion map, so that morphisms to an allowed output module are naturally the corresponding Ward maps. Its representing object is the Ward output; scalar conformal-block identities or a pentagon on spectral labels alone do not supply this universal property.
Weak factorization system of categories
Such a system gives categories over finite configuration spaces, compatible parameter pullbacks and external fusion on disjoint configurations, together with coherent unit and partition maps. In the weak form used here, external fusion on the whole categories need not be an equivalence, although the specified vacuum comparisons for surjections and disjoint fusion are required to be invertible.
Weak module
A module for a vertex algebra whose fields satisfy vectorwise lower truncation and the vertex-module identities, with no prescribed conformal grading, positive-energy bound or finite-dimensionality. For the finitely generated current presentations used here, sufficiently high modes kill each individual vector.
Weight-preserving operadic augmentation
An operadic augmentation is a morphism from an operad to the identity operad, which has only its identity operation in arity one. For an integer-weighted operad it is weight-preserving when every nonzero-weight element maps to zero and the identity has weight zero. A strict algebra unit together with multiplication can obstruct such an augmentation.
Weightwise complete lattice
For formal ℏ\hbar of weight −1-1, the completion has the form M=⨁w∏j≥0ℏjM0[w+j]M=\bigoplus_w\prod_{j\ge0}\hbar^jM_0[w+j]. Boundedness below and finite type mean respectively that M0[w]=0M_0[w]=0 below a lower bound and that each M0[w]M_0[w] is finite-dimensional; neither permits an unrestricted product over all weights.
Weil–Petersson metric and form
For harmonic Beltrami representatives on a closed hyperbolic surface, the full Weil–Petersson Hermitian pairing used here is H(μ,ν)=∫μνdAH(\mu,\nu)=\int\mu\overline\nu\,dA. Its form is ωWP=iHjk‾dtj∧dt‾k\omega_{\mathrm{WP}}=iH_{j\bar k}\,dt_j\wedge d\bar t_k. This normalization fixes the scale c/(24π)c/(24\pi) in the projective-immersion criterion.
Weil–Petersson quasicircle
A quasicircle is the image of the circle under a quasiconformal map. A normalized exterior univalent map belongs to the Weil–Petersson class when its Grunsky operator is Hilbert–Schmidt. This universal welding domain is distinct from the Teichmüller space of a fixed closed surface.
Wheel locus
For a scalar kernel γ\gamma, draw a directed edge i→ji\to j at a configuration when γ(Zj,Zi)=0\gamma(Z_j,Z_i)=0. The wheel locus is the locus of configurations with a directed cycle, or its image in the symmetric configuration space; it can lie away from ordinary collision diagonals.
